title: Dual Mesh Benchmark: Preregistered Latency and Integrity Measurements for Deterministic Anomaly-to-Playbook Resolution (Public Edition v2.0 — cross-platform verification appendix)
description:
The v1.0 record reported a preregistered benchmark of Squirrel OS's Dual Mesh deterministic resolution layer: the in-process mesh resolver resolved synthetic anomalies at a median of 0.000443 ms versus 4509.1 ms for the identical resolution task through an LLM conversation loop (ratio 1.018e+07, n=200/20), with mesh ingestion integrity (50/50 unique collision hashes) and resolution correctness (72/72 replay, zero false positives) verified.

Version 2.0 adds a cross-platform verification appendix. The same frozen corpus (sha256 13295d197be59dd1266814bc2f961f1e55e974c61c642fd9c7a6a389668fee59) was re-run under a second preregistered protocol: (1) mesh parity re-run confirming run-over-run determinism (200/200, median 0.00039 ms); (2) the LLM baseline leg re-executed from a second host (Cloudflare Workers edge, 20/20 valid, median 7.386 s, ratio 1.894e+07); and (3) the same task issued to an external LLM API substrate (OpenRouter, deepseek-chat, 20/20 valid, median 179.4 ms, ratio 4.60e+05). The mesh lookup outperforms both substrates on every measured host. The platform-loop wall-clock is shown to be dominated by conversation orchestration rather than model inference (~41x difference).

All amendments (host swap, output-fence normalization, rate-limit retry policy) were committed to the public ledger before the respective execution or re-attempt; strict first-pass scores are reported alongside normalized scores, and all raw runs are preserved verbatim in the evidence bundle. Claims remain scoped to the measured environments; no universal performance claim is made. All test data are synthetic; no production, customer, or personal data are involved. This software is a prototype and is provided for educational and research purposes only. It is not intended for production use, commercial deployment, or safety-critical environments. All systems are experimental and may contain defects on them.
